entity.name: Sigmund Freud
entity.description: The father of psychoanalysis who introduced the concepts of the unconscious mind, the id/ego/superego, and the Oedipus complex. His ideas pervaded 20th-century culture even as many were later challenged by science.

story.name: Sigmund Freud
story.description: Born in Moravia, dissecting eels in Trieste, inventing psychoanalysis at Berggasse 19 in Vienna, fleeing the Nazis to London, and dying in exile. The life of the man who tried to map the unconscious mind.

moments.name: Sigmund Freud Is Born in a Locksmith's Rented Room in Moravia
moments.subtitle: A wool merchant's struggling family produces the man who will reshape how humanity understands itself
moments.description: On 6 May 1856, Sigmund Freud was born to Ashkenazi Jewish parents Jakob and Amalia Freud in a rented room at Schlossergasse 117 in Freiberg, Moravia (now Pribor, Czech Republic). Jakob was a wool merchant on hard times; Amalia was his third wife, 20 years his junior. The infant was born with a caul, which his mother took as a positive omen. In 1859, the family left Freiberg for Leipzig and then Vienna, where Freud would spend nearly eight decades. The house where Freud was born is now a museum dedicated to his life and work.

moments.name: Freud Opens His Practice at Berggasse 19 and Invents Psychoanalysis
moments.subtitle: A Vienna apartment becomes the birthplace of free association, dream analysis, and the talking cure
moments.description: In 1891, Sigmund Freud moved his family and private practice into an apartment at Berggasse 19 in Vienna's Innere Stadt district. Over the next 47 years, this address became the birthplace of psychoanalysis. Here Freud developed free association, dream interpretation, and the theory of the unconscious. He received patients on his famous couch, hosted the Wednesday Psychological Society meetings that launched the psychoanalytic movement, and wrote most of his major works. Freud lived and worked at Berggasse 19 until June 1938, when the Nazi annexation of Austria forced him into exile. The apartment is now the Sigmund Freud Museum.

moments.name: A Young Freud Dissects Hundreds of Eels Searching for Their Testicles
moments.subtitle: The future explorer of the human psyche spends four weeks hunting for eel reproductive organs and finds nothing
moments.description: In 1876, 20-year-old medical student Sigmund Freud traveled to Carl Claus's zoological research station in Trieste, on the Adriatic coast. His assignment: find the male reproductive organs of eels, a mystery that had stumped biologists for centuries. Freud spent four weeks dissecting hundreds of eels but reached no conclusive results. The experience was one of Freud's earliest encounters with scientific frustration. The eel's reproductive system remained a mystery until the early 20th century. Ironically, the man who would build his career on theories of sexuality began with a failed search for sex organs in fish.

moments.name: Freud Flees Nazi-Occupied Vienna for London at Age 82
moments.subtitle: The Gestapo lets the dying father of psychoanalysis leave, but four of his sisters perish in the Holocaust
moments.description: On 4 June 1938, 82-year-old Sigmund Freud boarded the Orient Express in Vienna, fleeing Austria after the Nazi annexation. Despite his fame, Freud had been reluctant to leave until the Gestapo detained and interrogated his daughter Anna. With help from influential supporters including Princess Marie Bonaparte, Freud was allowed to emigrate to London with his immediate family. He settled at 20 Maresfield Gardens in Hampstead, where he continued seeing patients despite advanced jaw cancer from decades of cigar smoking. Four of Freud's sisters remained behind and later perished in Nazi concentration camps. Freud died in London on 23 September 1939, just weeks after World War II began.

moments.name: Sigmund Freud Dies by Physician-Assisted Morphine in London Exile
moments.subtitle: After 16 years and 33 operations for jaw cancer, the 83-year-old asks his doctor to end his suffering
moments.description: On 23 September 1939, Sigmund Freud died at his home at 20 Maresfield Gardens in Hampstead, London. Suffering from inoperable oral cancer caused by decades of cigar smoking, Freud had endured 33 surgeries over 16 years and was in constant pain. He reminded his physician Max Schur of a prior agreement, saying it was now nothing but torture and made no sense. Schur administered doses of morphine that ended Freud's life at age 83, just three weeks after Britain declared war on Germany. Freud was cremated at Golders Green Crematorium. His London home is now the Freud Museum, housing his library, antiquities collection, and the original psychoanalytic couch.
